newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Amoco to cut staff in Russian oil projects.
newsitem.headline: Amoco to cut staff in Russian oil projects.

text.p: Amoco Corp. said Tuesday it would cut staff on its multi-billion dollar Russian oil projects due to Moscow's slow progress in passing adequate tax and natural resource laws.

Dan Westbrook, senior vice-president and resident manager of Chicago-based Amoco's Amoco Eurasia Petroleum Co. subsidiary, told a news conference that "a slower than anticipated pace in the development of legislative and tax issues" was behind the cuts.
He did not say how many staff were affected, but stressed they were all Moscow-based.
He said the company, part of two large production-sharing projects, remained committed to doing business in Russia.
"We have not dropped any of our Russia projects," Westbrook said, adding that Amoco was pursuing deals and aimed to give the Russian side a 50 percent stake in each of them.

Russia has a production-sharing law but has not yet amended it to mesh with other legislation or smoothed out tax issues. It has not yet passed a list detailing which reserves are open to production-sharing.
